feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the positioning is clear, the career progression is logical, and the content shows solid scope across strategy, platforms, and operations. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and could be tighter, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that slightly reduce impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director, which builds credibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators and specifics (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, analytics stack, studio buildout), which strengthens impact.  
- Broad but coherent skill profile spanning strategy, CMS/web execution, analytics, and multimedia—well aligned to the target title.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; the CV repeats similar themes and tools too often.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities, especially in the freelance role and earlier positions (e.g., traffic growth, engagement gains, efficiency improvements, revenue/member impact).  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs versions without it); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French: A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and foregrounding public-sector/advocacy relevance would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct punctuation.
- Lead with your niche and seniority: public-sector/mission-driven digital strategy, cross-channel leadership, and platform modernization.
- Add one concrete differentiator from recent roles, such as enterprise web transformation, governance, or analytics-enabled decision-making.
- Trim broad phrases like “building the workflows and systems” in favor of sharper wording.

Suggested rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and workflow design. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused content and aligning stakeholders around effective advocacy and communications strategies.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow design/systems,” and “advocacy messaging” are repeated heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize higher-value leadership capabilities over broad or repeated phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic items like “Multi-channel communication” with more senior, specific phrasing such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Align wording with recent experience: emphasize platform modernization, digital governance, CMS strategy, analytics, and AI-enabled/content discovery work.
- Reduce repetition by combining overlapping items: “Workflow & systems architecture” and “Editorial workflow design” could become “Editorial workflows, governance & systems design.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS strategy • Editorial workflows, governance & systems design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, video & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, cross-channel communications, analytics, and stakeholder coordination.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills; consider keeping it in only one place.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground the highest-impact work, and add outcomes or scale where possible.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opener with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, with emphasis on Drupal modernization, cross-channel governance, and AI-enabled search.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Rephrase technical bullets to show business value: “Developed Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits to support advocacy and engagement goals.”
- Add measurable outcomes wherever available: site traffic, number of properties/pages supported, publishing efficiency gains, search/discovery improvements, or stakeholder/user adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with the footer project highlights; keep the CV entry focused on role-level leadership and outcomes, not detailed project descriptions.
- Avoid repeating governance/analytics/platform modernization language already used heavily in the NACo Director role unless you can show a new scale or result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good platform and scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the highest-impact achievement: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused: add growth, engagement, production volume, or efficiency metrics for newsletters/social if available; otherwise shorten to one line.
- Tighten the rest into impact verbs: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” / “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting stack…” / “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-functional planning systems…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program expansion may duplicate older NACo bullets unless framed here as studio-building and organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational leadership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth before the larger-scale modernization work.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite opening to sharpen scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, frequency, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations point: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” echo the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the prior Digital Media Manager entry; distinguish by scale, ownership, or strategic impact.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector specialization rather than generic content terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for high-volume publishing
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel” to “Cross-channel” for a more senior, operational tone.
- Replace “messaging” with “communications” to align with leadership-level work shown in recent roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale instead of generic wording, e.g., “governance for 10,000+ page web ecosystems” rather than “editorial systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than the strategic/operational strengths demonstrated in recent roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and Core Competencies. For a topline skills section, make it tighter, more strategic, and aligned to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove older/lower-priority platforms unless they are job-target relevant; keep Drupal first, as it is most supported by recent experience.
- Drop “jQuery” from topline skills unless required for the role; it dates the profile and is better left in Technical + IT.
- Consider adding one higher-value phrase tied to recent work, e.g. “modular microsite development” or “structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences,” “workflow automation,” and “CMS modernization” already appear elsewhere; avoid repeating the exact same wording across sections.
- Platform names duplicate the Technical + IT section; use this area for summary capabilities, not a second inventory.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value analytical capabilities over repeating tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Put the most strategic items first: analytics infrastructure, KPI design, executive reporting; tools can sit in parentheses.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- If accurate, strengthen outcomes language by aligning with recent experience: “enterprise analytics infrastructure” or “decision-ready reporting” rather than generic “optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Consider shortening this section or using it to highlight interpretation/decision support rather than repeating the same platforms.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent operational scope rather than generic task terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the current list with: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Virtual production operations”
- Use stronger, less generic phrasing: swap “video production and editing” for “broadcast-quality video production” and “livestreaming” for “livestream and hybrid event delivery.”
- Consider adding scale if supportable elsewhere, e.g., “in-house studio production” or “recurring advocacy video programming,” to connect to proven outcomes.
- Keep this section tool/capability-focused; leave detailed examples and achievements to Work Experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production” and “livestream operations” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “Livestream studio workflows” also overlap with Technical + IT, so keep this version broader and more strategic.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. In a technical section, this should either add specificity or be consolidated.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and prioritize by relevance: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add level/context for the strongest platform only: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; enterprise governance)” to reinforce impact from recent roles.
- Consider renaming to “CMS & Web Platforms” for clearer scanning and consistency with the content.
- Keep only platforms here; leave modernization, APIs, and AI search in other technical sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” Topline Skills entry almost exactly.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the seniority of the rest of the CV unless it supports a notable project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use and modernize older terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Remove “jQuery” unless it is still materially relevant to current work; if kept, place last or label as “legacy support.”
- Consider grouping by function for clarity: “Front-end,” “Integrations,” “Deployment/automation,” “Tagging.”
- If space allows elsewhere, add evidence tied to recent roles/projects (e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation”) rather than leaving this as a bare list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same stack in both places.
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap conceptually with “Workflow automation”; keep the distinction technical/deployment-focused here.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and group by function.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as categorized systems, e.g.: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello, Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest/most relevant tools first: lead with Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier if automation is the point.
- Consider replacing generic collaboration tools with more systems-oriented phrasing: “Airtable databases and workflow systems • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello project workflows.”
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to outcomes instead of listing tools only, e.g. “Built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate to streamline editorial planning and publishing operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; keep only if central to workflow design.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/ownership implied by the recent NACo roles. It should emphasize enterprise email/engagement platforms rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with scope wording: Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation and member communications across Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic and Mailchimp
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to outcomes rather than here: e.g., supported newsletters reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in the NACo experience bullets.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution, not broad leadership claims: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/launch, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience growth, email/social performance, or production cadence.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and coached a digital media associate on day-to-day publishing and production.”
- If metrics exist, combine into one impact line: “Produced X livestreams/Y video updates and helped improve [traffic, engagement, turnaround time, or publishing consistency].”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry centered on hands-on production and early team formation.
- Avoid repeating broad multi-channel oversight already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and trim broad language about “supporting programs and policy work.”

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy priorities.”
- Add the standout media contribution in a second clause: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a tighter outcome-oriented line, e.g. “Produced digital and multimedia content to support member communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders, or types of research/projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production; later roles already cover web, video, email and multimedia leadership in more depth.
- Don’t repeat “first in-house digital team” or weekly video/livestream work here; keep this item centered on research coordination + first podcast launch.
